news.content: The UK is close to agreeing to provide defensive military support to Saudi Arabia as the kingdom faces repeated attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis. Prime Minister Andy Burnham is reportedly leaning toward offering assistance such as aerial refuelling and encouraging other countries to provide similar support.The aim would be to help Saudi Arabia counter Houthi attacks, stabilise the region and reduce risks to shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb strait. If approved, it would be one of Burnham’s first major military decisions since becoming prime minister in July.

news.title: GOLD | Stronger Dollar & Profit-Taking Pressure Gold as Middle East Risks Persist⏰ Gold is starting the week under moderate selling pressure after last week’s s
news.content: GOLD | Stronger Dollar & Profit-Taking Pressure Gold as Middle East Risks Persist⏰ Gold is starting the week under moderate selling pressure after last week’s strong recovery, with a firmer U.S. dollar and profit-taking weighing on the metal.🟠 The macro backdrop remains challenging. The Federal Reserve’s latest rate hike and expectations for additional tightening continue to support U.S. rates and the dollar. Current market pricing also shows meaningful expectations for another Fed move, although the exact probability varies by meeting and changes intraday, Reuters reports roughly a 55% probability of another hike in October in Monday’s pricing.🟠 At the same time, oil prices are falling again, with Brent down around 2% on Monday amid hopes for diplomatic progress and improving Saudi supply flows. That is important for gold because lower crude reduces some of the longer-term inflation pressure and can ease expectations for aggressive monetary tightening.🟠 Middle East tensions add another layer. ⚠️ Escalation can generate safe-haven demand for gold, but if it causes another sustained surge in oil, the inflationary consequences could push yields and rate expectations higher—eventually becoming a headwind for gold.⚠️ The important distinction is therefore between short-term geopolitical safe-haven buying and the longer-term inflation/rates effect of the conflict.🕯 SM Market Outlook: Short-term neutral-to-bearish while the dollar remains firm and profit-taking continues. Lower oil is limiting the downside, while renewed geopolitical escalation could quickly increase volatility and safe-haven demand.

news.content: FED’S GOOLSBEE: RATE CUTS POSSIBLE IF INFLATION HEADS TO 2%Fed’s Goolsbee remains optimistic inflation can return to the 2% target, provided demand does not overheat.He says the Fed currently has an inflation problem, not an employment problem, and wants convincing evidence that price pressures are fading.If inflation is clearly heading back toward 2%, Goolsbee says he would have “no problem” with interest rates coming down.

news.title: GOLD | Stronger Dollar & Profit-Taking Pressure Gold as Middle East Risks Persist⏰ Gold is starting the week under moderate selling pressure after last week’s s
news.content: GOLD | Stronger Dollar & Profit-Taking Pressure Gold as Middle East Risks Persist⏰ Gold is starting the week under moderate selling pressure after last week’s strong recovery, with a firmer U.S. dollar and profit-taking weighing on the metal.🟠 The macro backdrop remains challenging. The Federal Reserve’s latest rate hike and expectations for additional tightening continue to support U.S. rates and the dollar. Current market pricing also shows meaningful expectations for another Fed move, although the exact probability varies by meeting and changes intraday, Reuters reports roughly a 55% probability of another hike in October in Monday’s pricing.🟠 At the same time, oil prices are falling again, with Brent down around 2% on Monday amid hopes for diplomatic progress and improving Saudi supply flows. That is important for gold because lower crude reduces some of the longer-term inflation pressure and can ease expectations for aggressive monetary tightening.🟠 Middle East tensions add another layer. ⚠️ Escalation can generate safe-haven demand for gold, but if it causes another sustained surge in oil, the inflationary consequences could push yields and rate expectations higher—eventually becoming a headwind for gold.⚠️ The important distinction is therefore between short-term geopolitical safe-haven buying and the longer-term inflation/rates effect of the conflict.🕯 SM Market Outlook: Short-term neutral-to-bearish while the dollar remains firm and profit-taking continues. Lower oil is limiting the downside, while renewed geopolitical escalation could quickly increase volatility and safe-haven demand.

news.title: U.S. INDICES | Trump–Xi Summit & Iran Tensions Take Center Stage■ U.S. stock index futures are trading higher at the start of the week, supported by easing oil
news.content: U.S. INDICES | Trump–Xi Summit & Iran Tensions Take Center Stage■ U.S. stock index futures are trading higher at the start of the week, supported by easing oil prices and renewed strength in technology shares, while investors turn their attention to the upcoming U.S.–China summit. Nasdaq futures were up about 0.6% and S&P 500 futures around 0.4% in Monday trading.■ President Donald Trump is scheduled to host Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington on September 24. Trade and tariffs are expected to be central, alongside Taiwan, artificial intelligence, critical minerals and the Iran conflict. Markets will pay particular attention to whether the two sides can extend their existing tariff truce and reduce the risk of renewed trade restrictions.■ A constructive outcome could reduce trade uncertainty and support global risk sentiment, particularly technology and semiconductor stocks. ■ Conversely, renewed tariff threats or sharper disagreement over Taiwan or technology restrictions could increase volatility.⚠️ At the same time, Middle East risk remains elevated. U.S.–Iran tensions intensified over the weekend, while shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains heavily disrupted compared with pre-war levels. ⚠️ This keeps geopolitical risk-and its potential effect on oil and inflation-firmly in focus.📊 Fundamental Bias: Short-term supportive for USNAS100, SPX500 and US30 while oil remains under pressure. The Trump–Xi summit on September 24 becomes a major catalyst, while renewed Iran/Middle East escalation remains the main geopolitical downside risk.

news.title: 🇨🇳🇺🇸 China cuts US Treasury holdings to an 18-year low• China has been reducing its holdings for over a decade, down from around $1.3 trillion in the early
news.content: 🇨🇳🇺🇸 China cuts US Treasury holdings to an 18-year low• China has been reducing its holdings for over a decade, down from around $1.3 trillion in the early 2010s to $618 billion today.• The decline accelerated after 2022 as China became more concerned about relying too heavily on US assets.• Foreign governments are buying fewer US Treasuries, while hedge funds and other investors are buying more.• Weaker foreign demand is helping push Treasury yields higher, with the 30-year yield recently hitting a nearly 20-year high.• Higher yields mean the US government has to pay more to borrow money.

event_sources.original_content: GOLD | Stronger Dollar & Profit-Taking Pressure Gold as Middle East Risks Persist⏰ Gold is starting the week under moderate selling pressure after last week’s strong recovery, with a firmer U.S. dollar and profit-taking weighing on the metal.🟠 The macro backdrop remains challenging. The Federal Reserve’s latest rate hike and expectations for additional tightening continue to support U.S. rates and the dollar. Current market pricing also shows meaningful expectations for another Fed move, although the exact probability varies by meeting and changes intraday, Reuters reports roughly a 55% probability of another hike in October in Monday’s pricing.🟠 At the same time, oil prices are falling again, with Brent down around 2% on Monday amid hopes for diplomatic progress and improving Saudi supply flows. That is important for gold because lower crude reduces some of the longer-term inflation pressure and can ease expectations for aggressive monetary tightening.🟠 Middle East tensions add another layer. ⚠️ Escalation can generate safe-haven demand for gold, but if it causes another sustained surge in oil, the inflationary consequences could push yields and rate expectations higher—eventually becoming a headwind for gold.⚠️ The important distinction is therefore between short-term geopolitical safe-haven buying and the longer-term inflation/rates effect of the conflict.🕯 SM Market Outlook: Short-term neutral-to-bearish while the dollar remains firm and profit-taking continues. Lower oil is limiting the downside, while renewed geopolitical escalation could quickly increase volatility and safe-haven demand.

The Federal Reserve’s latest rate hike and expectations for additional tightening continue to support U.S. rates and the dollar. Current market pricing also shows meaningful expectations for another Fed move, although the exact probability varies by meeting and changes intraday, Reuters reports roughly a 55% probability of another hike in October in Monday’s pricing.🟠 At the same time, oil prices are falling again, with Brent down around 2% on Monday amid hopes for diplomatic progress and improving Saudi supply flows. That is important for gold because lower crude reduces some of the longer-term inflation pressure and can ease expectations for aggressive monetary tightening.🟠 Middle East tensions add another layer. ⚠️ Escalation can generate safe-haven demand for gold, but if it causes another sustained surge in oil, the inflationary consequences could push yields and rate expectations higher—eventually becoming a headwind for gold.⚠️ The important distinction is therefore between short-term geopolitical safe-haven buying and the longer-term inflation/rates effect of the conflict.🕯 SM Market Outlook: Short-term neutral-to-bearish while the dollar remains firm and profit-taking continues. Lower oil is limiting the downside, while renewed geopolitical escalation could quickly increase volatility and safe-haven demand.
